figures.finding: St Kitts and Nevis levies no income tax on individuals: the Income Tax Act (Chapter 20.22) charged individuals from 1967, but income tax on individuals was abolished in 1980; only companies pay it.

sources.said: The Income Tax Act was passed in 1966 and came into force on the first day of January 1967. It made provisions for income tax to be charged on both individuals and corporate entities. Income tax on individuals was abolished in 1980.
There is no individual income tax in St. Kitts and Nevis.

figures.finding: Employee and employer each pay 5% social security on monthly earnings up to XCD 6,500; the employer adds 1% employment injury, 3% housing and social development levy and 1% severance. The employee's housing and social development levy is 3.5% on monthly earnings from XCD 2,253.34 to 6,500, 10% to 8,000 and 12% above.
figures.applies: 2026; the levy (Housing and Social Development Levy Act Chap. 20.21) works as the tax on pay.
